elements.evidence: The added language states that Customer “may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right on 30 days’ notice.
elements.evidence: The added right is exercisable “upon 30 days' ... notice to Contractor.”

elements.element: Customer’s termination-for-convenience notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly requires “30 days' written notice.”

elements.element: Upon Customer’s termination for convenience, Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
elements.evidence: Contractor must “refund, on a pro-rata basis, any prepaid fees for Services not performed as of the effective date of termination.”

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Vendor’s existing convenience right applies only when “there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding,” and it does not permit Vendor to terminate an outstanding Statement of Work for convenience.
The added clause gives Customer an express right to terminate the Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience.

elements.element: Customer’s termination-for-convenience notice period is between 60 and 90 days.
elements.evidence: The added clause specifies 30 days’ notice, not a period within the required 60–90-day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months’ fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed; therefore, no fee exceeds the three-month cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Clause (a) permits Vendor to terminate “at any time” when no uncompleted Statement of Work is outstanding, rather than only at the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor must provide 90 days’ notice to terminate for convenience.
elements.evidence: Clause (a) allows Vendor to terminate on only 15 days’ advance notice.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred requirement: Customer receives a 30-day written convenience-termination right covering the Agreement and individual Statements of Work, with a pro-rata refund, while Contractor cannot exercise convenience termination while an uncompleted SOW is outstanding. The fallback is not independently satisfied because the Customer notice period is 30 rather than 60–90 days, and Contractor retains a 15-day right exercisable other than solely at term end. The drafting preserves the existing breach and payment provisions, but it is not minimal because the final sentence redundantly restates Customer’s convenience right and refers to an unlabeled “Paragraph 6(c),” reducing drafting quality.
